2024 
Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia  1 M.Cr.C.No.40838/2023 IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GURPAL SINGH AHLUWALIA  ON THE 13th OF APRIL, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 40838 of 2023 BETWEEN:- 
1. SATENDRA KUMAR S/O SHRI MEWA  RAM, AGED ABOUT 53 YEARS,
 OCCUPATION: SELF EMPLOYED R/O  705-D-16/2 WARD NO 03 NEAR  AAMBAGH MOHROLI NEW DELHI  MANDIR MARG NEW DELHI 2. SEEMA DEVI W/O SATENDRA  KUMAR, AGED ABOUT 55 YEARS,
 OCCUPATION: HOUSE WIFE R/O 705-  D-16/2, WARD NO.03, NEAR AAMBAGH  MOHROLI, NEW DELHI MANDIR  MARG, NEW DELHI (DELHI)
 .....APPLICANTS (BY SHRI VIVEK AGRAWAL - ADVOCATE )
AND 1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  THROUGH P.S. MAHILA THANA  BHOPAL CITY DISTRICT BHOPAL  (MADHYA PRADESH) 
2. SMT. NEETU OAD W/O SANJEEV  KUMAR, AGED ABOUT 31 YEARS, R/O  H.NO.63 ISHAAN PARK PATEL  NAGAR RAISEN ROAD, POLICE  STATION PIPLANI BHOPAL DISTRICT  BHOPAL (MADHYA PRADESH)

 ORDER This application under section 482 of CrPC has been filed seeking the following relief(s) :-
"It is therefore prayed to the Hon'ble Court may be please to allow the petition and quashed the FIR dated 03.06.2023 as well as charge sheet dated 26.06.2023 in relation with crime no.169/2023 further the consequences the entire proceeding pending before JMFC Bhopal District Bhopal be quashed and all subsequent proceeding pending be quashed, in the interest of justice." 
2. The applicant is the father-in-law; whereas the applicant no.2 is the mother-in-law of respondent no.2. The respondent no.2 lodged an FIR against the applicants as well as their son Sanjeev Kumar on the allegations that she got married to Sanjeev Kumar on 10.12.2022. The marriage expenses were borne by the parents of the girl and dowry to the satisfaction of the applicants as well as her husband was given. The situation was normal for 4 months after the marriage. Thereafter, the applicants and her husband started passing taunts on trivial issues. The applicants and her husband were scolding that her parents have not given anything good in the dowry; whereas her father is posted on a high post, therefore, she should bring an amount of Rs.5,00,000/-. When she replied that her parents have already given the dowry as per their financial capacity, then she was abused and assaulted by her husband. Her in-laws were compelling her to perform the entire house-hold work and were also not giving the adequate food for her survival. When she got pregnant even at that time she was abused and assaulted by her husband. She gave birth to a girl child then her husband as well as the applicants scolded her that they wanted a boy but she has given birth to a girl child. 
Thereafter the harassment by her husband and parents-in-law increased and they continuously started demanding an amount of Rs.5,00,000/-. They were insisting that unless and until she brings an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- from her parents, they will continue to harass her. The in-laws were not allowing her to talk to her parents on phone. When she tried to talk to her parents from her mobile phone, then her mobile phone was broken by the applicant no.1. She was tolerating the cruelty with a hope and belief that with the passage of time the things would improve and her matrimonial life would survive. On 5.5.2023 her husband as well as the applicants demanded dowry of Rs.5,00,000/-. When it was refused by her then she was abused and assaulted by her husband and she was asked to go out of the house. She tried to convince her husband as well as the applicants but the applicants and her husband did not agree and ultimately she was turned out of her house with a threat that in case if she comes back without an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- then she would be killed and accordingly it is alleged that she came back to her parental house along with her daughter and since then she is residing in her parental home. Neither her husband is coming to take her back to her matrimonial house nor he is talking to her. She was harassed mentally and with cruelty by the applicants as well as her husband for demand of Rs.5,00,000/- and accordingly it was prayed that Satendra Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199347337/
2 an action be taken against the applicants as well as against her husband.
3. By referring to a letter dated 4.5.2023 addressed to none, it is submitted that the respondent no.2 had left her matrimonial house by giving a written statement that because of dispute with her in-laws she is going back to her parental home along with her parents. 
4. It is submitted that this letter was executed on 4.5.2023, which clearly indicates that the allegation that on 5.5.2023 she was ousted from her matrimonial house after giving a beating, is false. 
5. Further by referring to a complaint filed by the applicant no.2 before SHO, Police Station,
Mehrauli dated 31.5.2021, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that applicant no.1 had already informed the SHO, Police Station Mehrauli that he has disowned his son as well as respondent no.2 because of their undesirable conduct and inappropriate behavior unbecoming of civilized citizen and they are not under the control of the applicants. Accordingly, an information was given that Sanjeev Kumar and the respondent no.2 are not under his control and authority and their actions and deeds are undesirable and inappropriate and henceforth if any person dealing with them in whatsoever circumstances shall be himself/herself/itself/themselves responsible and the applicant no.1 shall not be responsible for the same in any circumstances. 
6. The counsel for the applicants could not point out the reasons why the applicant no.1 disowned his own son. This information given by the applicant no.1 to SHO, Police Station, Mehrauli is dated 31.5.2021. In this information, the applicant no.1 has given his address as House No.705-D, 16/2,
Ward No.3, Mehrauli, New Delhi; whereas in the FIR the address of the husband of the respondent no.2 is also the same. 
7. It is further submitted by counsel for the applicants that even their son had given an information to the police on 4.5.2023 itself that today his in-laws have taken his wife back. However, it is suffice to mention here that this information does not contain any acknowledgment of receipt. 
8. Similarly, it is submitted by the counsel for applicants that on 5.5.2023 the applicant no.1 had also given an information that while they were not in house, the parents of the girl had forcibly taken away the girl (respondent no.2). It is suffice to mention here that even this complaint does not bear any acknowledgment of receipt. However, this complaint clearly throws a light on the fact that the son of the applicants is residing with the applicants because in complaint dated 5.5.2023 the applicant no.1 has specifically admitted that the applicants as well as his son are residing in the same house. 
9. Thus, it is clear that the son of the applicants is still residing with them. Once the son of the applicants is also residing with the applicants then giving of an information to Police Station Mehrauli on 31.5.2021 prima facie appears to be a defence to overcome an eventuality, which may arise in future. If the applicant no.1 was so disturbed with the uncivilized behavior of his son then why he was not ousted from the house. 
Satendra Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199347337/
3 10. Thus, it is clear that applicant no.1 was deliberately and in a planned manner was preparing false defence. The necessity of preparing false defence, by itself indicates that applicants had guilty mind. 
11. So far as the contention of the counsel for applicants that as per the written declaration dated 4.5.2023 the respondent no.2 had left her matrimonial house on 4.5.2023; whereas as per the FIR,
the incident took place on 5.5.2023, therefore, it is clear that no incident had taken place on 5.5.2023 is concerned, it is suffice to mention here that even in the written declaration it was specifically mentioned that the relationship are strained. What was the need of giving an information to the Police Station Mehrauli, New Delhi, is a question, which is to be explained by the applicants in the trial. The written declaration is not addressed to anybody. Therefore, it is prima facie clear that the respondent no.2 must not have gone to the Police Station Mehrauli, New Delhi to give information about her departure from the matrimonial house. 
12. Since it is a private document, therefore, it is required to be proved and this Court cannot take cognizance of the same in support of the defence of the applicants. 
13. So far as the discrepancy with regard to the date of incident as to whether the respondent no.2 was ousted from her matrimonial house on 4.5.2023 or 5.5.2023, it is suffice to mention here that undue importance cannot be given to such a discrepancy and it shall be open for the complainant to explain the discrepancy and if it is found that the explanation given by the complainant is plausible then the same can be relied upon. There are specific allegations of harassment, passing of taunts and breaking of mobile phone by the applicants or applicant no.1.
14. The Supreme Court in the case of Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held as under:-
"12. In Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P. [Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P., (2014) 16 SCC 551] , it was observed (SCC p. 553, paras 8-9):
"8. We have gone through the FIR and the criminal complaint. In the FIR, the appellants have not been named and in the criminal complaint they have been named without attributing any specific role to them. The relationship of the appellants with the husband of the complainant is distant. In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab [Kans Raj v.
State of Punjab, (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662] it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5):
"5. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in-laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits. In their overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case." 
Satendra Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199347337/
4 The Court has, thus, to be careful in summoning distant relatives without there being specific material. Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations. Mere naming of distant relations is not enough to summon them in the absence of any specific role and material to support such role. 
9. The parameters for quashing proceedings in a criminal complaint are well known. If there are triable issues, the Court is not expected to go into the veracity of the rival versions but where on the face of it, the criminal proceedings are abuse of Court's process, quashing jurisdiction can be exercised. Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar [K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar, (2000) 8 SCC 547 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 27] , Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate [Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 :
1998 SCC (Cri) 1400] , State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal [State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 :
1992 SCC (Cri) 426 : AIR 1992 SC 604] and Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P.
[Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P., (2011) 11 SCC 259 : (2011) 3 SCC (Cri) 159] "
13. In the present case, the complaint is as follows:
"Sir, it is submitted that I was married on 18- 11-2009 with Sidharath Parakh s/o Manak Chand Parakh r/o Sarafa Bazar in front of Radha Krishna Market, Gwalior according to the Hindu rites and customs. In the marriage my father had given gold and silver ornaments, cash amount and household goods according to his capacity. 
After the marriage when I went to my matrimonial home, I was treated nicely by the members of the family. When on the second occasion I went to my matrimonial home, my husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law started harassing me for not bringing the dowry and started saying that I should bring from my father 25-30 tolas of gold and Rs 2,00,000 in cash and only then they would keep me in the house otherwise not. On account of this my husband also used to beat me and my father-in-law and my mother-in-law used to torture me by giving the taunts. In this connection I used to tell my father Kundanmal Oswal, my mother Smt Prem Lata Oswal, uncle Ashok Rai Sharma and uncle Ved Prakash Mishra from time to time. On 2-4-2010 the members of the family of my matrimonial home forcibly sent me to the house of my parents in Ganj Basoda along with my brother Deepak. They snatched my clothes and ornaments and kept with them. Since then till today my husband has been harassing me on the telephone and has not come to take me back. Being compelled, I have been moving this application before you. Sir, it is prayed that Satendra Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199347337/
5 action be taken against husband Sidharath Parakh, my father-in-law Manak Chand Parakh and my mother-in-law Smt Indira Parakh for torturing me on account of demanding dowry."
14. From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out. There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home. Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home. The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out. Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible." 
15. The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Abhishek Vs. State of M.P., decided on 31st August, 2023 in Criminal Appeal No.1457/2015 to submit that the proceedings can be quashed, if these proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive of wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances the High Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely. It is further submitted that the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection, to try and read between the lines. 
16. If the facts of the present case are concerned, this Court has already considered that what was the need for the respondent no.2 to give in writing before leaving her matrimonial house. That shows that the relationship was strained. Even otherwise in the written declaration, it was specifically mentioned by the respondent no.2 that on account of dispute with her in-laws she is going back to her parental home. Furthermore, the applicants have also not explained that once the applicant no.1 has disowned his son Sanjeev Kumar then why Sanjeev Kumar was allowed to stay in the house of the applicants itself. 
17. Thus considering the circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is a prima facie case warranting prosecution of the applicants no.1 and 2.
18. Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference. 
19. The application fails and is hereby dismissed. 
(G.S.AHLUWALIA) JUDGE TG/-

annotations.text: From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out.
There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home.
Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home.
The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out.
Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible."

15. The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Abhishek Vs. State of M.P., decided on 31st August, 2023 in Criminal Appeal No.1457/2015 to submit that the proceedings can be quashed, if these proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive of wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances the High Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.

It is further submitted that the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection, to try and read between the lines.
16. If the facts of the present case are concerned, this Court has already considered that what was the need for the respondent no.2 to give in writing before leaving her matrimonial house.
That shows that the relationship was strained.
Even otherwise in the written declaration, it was specifically mentioned by the respondent no.2 that on account of dispute with her in-laws she is going back to her parental home.
Furthermore, the applicants have also not explained that once the applicant no.1 has disowned his son Sanjeev Kumar then why Sanjeev Kumar was allowed to stay in the house of the applicants itself.

17. Thus considering the circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is a prima facie case warranting prosecution of the applicants no.1 and 2.

The Court has, thus, to be careful in summoning distant relatives without there being specific material.
Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations.
